gazulus: Benedetto has asked whether the stars favour the voyage. He has already hired the ship, so I imagine they had better.
You may trust his arithmetic. It is the little sentence beneath the arithmetic that requires attention.
He speaks as though bread travels from a field to a hungry man by the unaided grace of merchants. Still, it does arrive.
Benedetto is absent? Then we may discuss a matter without discovering that someone has already purchased it.
I have told him that a promise is binding even when no notary hears it. He asked whether the notary's fee could then be omitted.
He knows a captain for every difficulty. Ask who pays the captain if the difficulty becomes Turkish.
Benedetto says I take too long to answer. He has never had to bring a sentence home through three hostile courts.
His letters from Naples are useful. Read the account of the harbour before the account of his reception at court.
The Senate has given me precise instructions. Benedetto will be pleased; precise instructions have edges one can work around.
Do not mistake his bargaining for indifference. He dislikes waste, and a city full of people is a considerable thing to waste.
Yesterday he called our caution expensive. I asked him to price another war. He has been quieter this morning.
If he offers to settle the matter privately, ask what he intends to say when it becomes public. He usually has an answer.
cotrugli: Master Gazulus is still considering your request. A promising sign: he has stopped explaining why it cannot be considered.
Ask him what the Senate permits. Then ask me what the ship can carry. Those are separate questions; we prefer to keep them so.
He told me the heavens do not revolve around trade. I agreed. It saved a morning, and neither of us lost a customer.
When Gazulus says 'regrettably', stay seated. There are usually another two paragraphs before you learn what he has actually refused.
He knows kings, cardinals and the distances between stars. I know a warehouse with a sound roof. Today you may need us both.
He has made me remove the word 'guaranteed'. Fair enough. I had not yet spoken to the captain.
Gazulus thinks a seal improves a letter. I find it improves the price of carrying it through a blockade.
Our learned friend worries what will be written about us. I worry who will still be here to read it.
He has found a lawful objection. Give him a moment; he takes almost as much pleasure in finding a lawful way round it.
Do listen when he mentions the war at home. I complain about cautious men, but I do not offer to bury their sons.
He calls this a charitable undertaking. I have agreed to leave that heading in the accounts, provided the expenses may follow it.
You will get no rash promise from Gazulus. That is inconvenient at the table and comforting once you have left it.
